chief_complaint: bright blood-red patch on white part of eyeball discovered in mirror after violent coughing spell without pain or visual change
hpi_details: 55M presenting with alarming bright red sector hemorrhage beneath bulbar conjunctiva stopping at limbus after coughing fit where vision, pupils, and fundus are completely normal managed with reassurance and artificial tears as blood reabsorbs over 2 weeks.
ideas: He thinks he burst an important blood vessel in his eye from straining during his violent coughing fit.
concerns: He is worried that this is a warning sign that a blood vessel might burst in his brain and cause a stroke.
expectations: He hopes the doctor will check his eye and give him special drops to quickly dissolve the pool of blood.

reference_soap.plan: If vision, pupils, and the remainder of the eye examination are normal and there is no significant trauma, provide reassurance and optional artificial tears for comfort; the blood usually clears over 1 to 2 weeks. Check blood pressure and review anticoagulant use when indicated. Arrange prompt assessment for pain, photophobia, reduced vision, significant trauma, recurrent episodes, or other bleeding symptoms.

red_flags: Recurrent episodes would warrant a bleeding disorder or blood pressure workup

must_ask.objective: Confirm painless and no vision change
must_ask.say: Is there any pain, or has your vision changed at all?
Did this happen right after coughing, sneezing, or straining?

must_ask.objective: Screen for blood thinner use or bleeding disorders
must_ask.say: Do you take any blood thinners like aspirin or warfarin, or have any bleeding problems?
With a normal eye examination, this is usually harmless and clears on its own over about one to two weeks. Seek care promptly if you develop pain or vision changes.

history.answer: I looked in the bathroom mirror this morning and was shocked to see a solid, bright red pool of blood covering the white of my right eye.
I first noticed it right after I woke up and looked in the mirror around seven o'clock this morning. It is only in my right eye, and it hasn't spread or changed since.
It is a distinct, solid patch of bright red blood on the outer white portion of my eyeball. The dark, colored part of my eye looks completely clear.
No, there is no pain at all, not even an ache or deep soreness. My eye just feels slightly heavy when I blink, but it doesn't hurt.
No, my vision is completely clear and normal. I can read and see across the room just as well as yesterday.
No, bright light does not bother my eyes at all.
No, I haven't seen any colored halos or rings around lights, and I have had no headache, nausea, or vomiting.
No discharge, yellow pus, or stickiness at all. My eyelids were completely clean and not stuck together when I woke up.
No, my eye does not itch, and I haven't had the urge to rub it.
No, my eyelids are not swollen, and there are no bumps, crusting, or burning along my eyelashes.
No, my eye moves smoothly in every direction without any pain, neither eye looks pushed out, and I have no double vision or fever.
I had a sudden, violent coughing fit late yesterday evening after choking on a sip of water. I haven't had a cold, fever, or anyone around me with pink eye.
No, I have never worn contact lenses. I only use reading glasses when reading small print.
No, I didn't hit my eye, poke it, or get any foreign particles or chemicals splashed into it.
No, I have never suffered from seasonal allergies, hay fever, asthma, or atopic dermatitis.
No, my eyes don't feel dry or gritty, and I haven't had dry mouth or excessive screen fatigue.
No, I do not have any morning back stiffness, swollen joints, mouth ulcers, or chronic bowel issues.
No, I have never had shingles, cold sores, or any blisters on my forehead or nose.
I don't lift heavy weights or strain with bowel movements, but that coughing fit last night was very forceful.
No, I don't bruise easily, and I haven't had any nosebleeds, bleeding gums, or blood in my stool or urine.
No, I have never had glaucoma, serious eye conditions, or any bleeding like this in my eye before.
I thought I must have popped a major vein in my eyeball when I was coughing so hard. I'm terrified that if a vessel broke in my eye, another one might burst in my head and give me a stroke.

I was hoping you could prescribe some drops to clear this blood away quickly so my eye looks normal again.
I don't have any major chronic medical conditions, and my doctor has never told me I have high blood pressure or diabetes.
I had an appendectomy when I was in college, but I have never had eye surgery or any other hospital stays.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter blood thinners, aspirin, or dietary supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medications or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only drink one or two beers on the weekend with friends, and none during the work week.
I work as an office accountant and live with my wife. My home and work environments are quiet and stable.
No one in my family has a history of eye diseases, early glaucoma, or bleeding and clotting disorders.

exam.finding: Calm, well-appearing man in no acute distress, sitting comfortably without grimacing or covering his eyes.
Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.6 °C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Uncorrected visual acuity 20/20 in each eye, round pupils equally reactive to light with no afferent pupillary defect, full extraocular movements without pain or proptosis, and normal funduscopy.

Sharply demarcated bright red sector hemorrhage beneath the temporal bulbar conjunctiva of the right eye terminating precisely at the limbus, with a clear cornea, deep anterior chamber, and normal left eye.
No skin petechiae, ecchymoses, abnormal hematomas, or rash on the face or body.
